content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text treats the defender's answers and the challenger's pressed witnesses as two opposing chains, so K-C governs how that collision is weighed.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.","rule_words":"the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"Whether \"neither chain forces the other\" is a chain-against-chain result or a retired stating-verse test; I read it as chain-against-chain because the text expressly sets the two chains against each other and does not say no individual verse states the contrary.","why":"The judge text resolves the collision as chain against chain and does not rely on the retired no-single-verse-states-contrary test, so it obeys K-C."}
